title: Module change risk catalog and registry workflow
content:
DRAFT: Module change risk catalog + registry publishing workflow

Purpose:
- Provide a concise operational playbook for publishing Terraform modules used in Private deployment bundles (VPC/on-prem).
- Capture risk classes for changes, required automated / manual gates, and an opinionated registry publishing checklist focused on artifact provenance and safe upgrades.

Scope:
- Applies to all terraform modules that ship in our Private product manifests, module namespace redwood-inference/*, and any on-prem distribution bundles.
- Does NOT replace per-customer emergency patch procedures; those are in the incident runbook.

Quick summary of the approach:
1) Classify change -> 2) Run gated tests -> 3) Produce signed artifact + provenance metadata -> 4) Publish to registry (staged) -> 5) Canary promotion -> 6) Monitor and rollback if needed

Definitions / risk classes (keep simple and actionable):
- Low (patch): Non-behavioural edits, docs, formatting, variable defaults that are backwards compatible, provider pin bumps within a minor version that are known-safe.
- Medium (minor): New optional resources/outputs, additional variables with defaults, refactors that preserve interfaces. Requires plan/regression test across example stacks.
- High (major): Anything that changes default behaviour, removes or renames exported outputs/inputs, changes state layout, or alters resource names. Requires migration guides and customer outreach.

Semver rules we follow (opinionated):
- Major version bump (vX+1.0.0): incompatible changes. Must be explicit and accompanied by migration docs, TF plan diffs for representative stacks, and a 2-week heads-up to internal consumers.
- Minor bump (vX.Y+1.0): new functionality that is additive and opt-in. Tests must show zero diffs for existing example stacks.
- Patch (vX.Y.Z+1): non-behavioural fixes. Can be published automatically after CI and signed-artifact checks.

Provenance and immutability (non-negotiable):
- Every published artefact must include: git tag, commit SHA, built-by CI id, build log link, sha256 of packaged module, and PGP signature from the release pipeline.
- Registry blobs are immutable; to fix a published issue, publish a new semver version (no force updates). If an immediate emergency patch is needed, follow emergency-meeting and opt for a major version with compatibility shim if required.

CI gating checklist (automated where possible):
- terraform fmt and validate across supported TF versions (we test 1.1, 1.2, 1.5 in CI matrix).
- unit checks: terratest/unit mocks (where present) -> pass.
- plan-only runs for each canonical example stack pinned to realistic provider versions. Compare plan diff against approved baseline; disallow unexpected destroys on default stacks.
- integration test: apply to ephemeral account/VPC, smoke test resource creation, then destroy. Retain logs for 7 days.
- state-migration simulation: for high-risk changes, run import + plan on a snapshot of an existing example state to show diffs.

Manual gates (when required):
- API breaking changes or renames = product owner and platform-ops signoff.
- Security-sensitive changes (new IAM policies, service account perms) require security review and short threat-model note.
- Performance-sensitive changes (e.g., switching provisioners that change timing) need an ops perf run.

Registry publish workflow (step-by-step):
1) Create a release branch: release/<module>-vX.Y.Z including CHANGELOG entry and RELEASE_NOTES.md.
2) CI builds packaged module artifact tar.gz, calculates sha256, attaches PGP signature.
3) CI submits artifact to staging registry namespace: staging.redwood-registry/private/<module>/vX.Y.Z with metadata JSON.
4) Run automated smoke tests against staging registry (downstream consumer install + plan).
5) Manual review: reviewer checks provenance metadata, plan diffs, and example stacks for unexpected changes.
6) If green, promote artifact to prod registry via controlled promotion pipeline (no direct writes). Promotion creates a signed audit entry and notifies #release-notifications.
7) Post-publish: tag upstream repo with annotated tag and update internal manifests that pin the released version.

Canary promotion and monitoring plan:
- For medium/high risk modules we use staged promotion: 5% of internal bundles (by customer or test cluster) are pinned to new module version for 48 hours. Monitor: apply success rate, drift, errors in plan/apply, and any increase in support tickets.
- Telemetry hooks: record module version, change-class, and CI id in logs so postmortems can correlate.

Rollback and mitigation patterns (playbook):
- Immediate rollback: if canary fails (>=2 critical failures in 24h), revert consumers to previous module version in manifests and trigger infra-runner job to re-run apply. Notify customers on relevant private deployments.
- Forward-fix: if defect is isolated and fixable quickly, publish vX.Y.Z+1 patch with migration shim.
- Emergency major: if state-destructive bug found post-publish, assemble emergency response, publish clear migration steps, and consider a compatibility wrapper module that maps old inputs to new behaviour.

Pre-publish checklist (copyable):
- [ ] CHANGELOG entry present and clear (impact, mitigation, required actions)
- [ ] Release notes drafted (include example plan diffs)
- [ ] Automated CI matrix green for supported TF versions
- [ ] Signed artifact and sha256 checksum generated
- [ ] Staging registry smoke tests passed
- [ ] Security review completed (if new permissions)
- [ ] Product/PO acknowledged consumer impact (for minor/major changes)
- [ ] Migration guide in docs/ if needed

Communication templates (brief):
- Internal release note (Slack): "module x published vX.Y.Z -> staged->prod. Risk class: Medium. CI: <CI run link>. If you have pinned stacks, please test and report by EOD +48h."
- Customer advisory (short): subject: "Redwood module X: planned upgrade available". Body: summary of change, required action, safe pining instructions, contact support link.

Example semantic decision table (quick):
- Change: add new optional output -> Minor. Tests: plan must be no-diff for existing stacks. Docs: update outputs table.
- Change: rename var or remove output -> Major. Tests: migration plan + state-sim. Communication: 2-week notice.
- Change: bump provider minor patch -> Patch if no behavioral change; else Minor.

Notes on TF provider and versioning complexities (lessons learned):
- Provider deprecations sometimes silently change behaviours; pin provider ranges in examples and run provider-upgrade tests in a separate CI job.
- Avoid using 'count' vs 'for_each' swaps that change resource addressing without migration shims. If unavoidable, provide a mapping script in tools/ that can be used in-state migration.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define retention and visibility for signed build logs (we keep 7 days — is that enough for audits?).
- Should we enforce PGP signing from a central HSM rather than CI worker key? Security leaning strongly to HSM but requires infra work.
- Can we extend canary automation to pick real customer non-prod clusters instead of static internal ones? Privacy concerns need review.

Appendix: quick commands and examples:
- Build artifact locally (dev flow): git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "release" && ./scripts/package-module.sh | tee build.log
- Verify checksum: sha256sum module-vX.Y.Z.tar.gz
- Promote from staging (ops pipeline): ./scripts/promote.sh --module <name> --from staging --to prod --ci-id <ci run>

Notes-to-self (rough):
- Keep this doc short and practical, link out to deeper migration docs.
- Iterate after next 2 releases to capture friction points.

End of draft.
